title: Wave computation serializes cells sharing a regen-obligation root
action: PBI p-50f3af4d (verified: compute_schedule at schedule.rs:34-100 groups purely by declared schedule_files_of; obligation.rs derives regen obligations but scheduling never consults it; recurred 3x as write-time conflicts): two cells whose declared files are disjoint but which BOTH trigger a regen obligation over the same obligated root (e.g. both touch skills/ subtrees -> both owe the render-trees/onboard-apply/manifest chain) land in the same wave and then collide on the whole-tree regen. Fix in schedule.rs: when computing overlap for wave placement, derive each cell's obligated regen roots through the SAME derivation obligation.rs/cells-add uses (reuse the function — never a hand-kept root list), and treat two cells sharing at least one obligated root as conflicting exactly like a file overlap, so they auto-serialize into different waves. Cells with disjoint files and no shared obligation keep byte-identical wave placement. The schedule output's conflict reason names the shared obligated root (so the orchestrator sees WHY they serialized). TDD red-first: two cells with disjoint files both touching manifest-hashed roots land in different waves with the root named (red today: same wave); disjoint cells without shared obligations pin byte-identical waves; cycle detection unchanged.

truths: two disjoint-file cells sharing an obligated regen root serialize into different waves with the root named
cells without shared obligations keep byte-identical wave placement
obligated roots derive from the existing obligation derivation, never a hand list

trace.outcome: compute_schedule derives obligated roots via derive_regen_guards (the cells-add authority) and serializes shared-root cells like file overlaps; obligation_conflicts recorded on the Schedule struct
deviations: conflict rendering in the cells schedule command was out of the declared file scope - completed by follow-up cell sra-2
